locator: §5.2, 'If this can be defended, we can distinguish minimalist and nonminimalist uses of the terms and ideas in question.'
interpretation: Dreier's proposal (2018) for keeping the minimal/robust contrast after the collapse argument: the non-minimal reading of truth and truth conditions is the realist one, on which they explain our thought and talk. Read as: if a moral sentence is robustly truth-apt, its truth conditions explain our thought and talk with it. Only this direction is formalized. The entry gives the proposal conditionally ('if this can be defended') and adds that it may undercut the non-cognitivist's further use of minimalism; the claim records the proposal, not its defense. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
